sentence: This project studies how gene control changes drive oxidative stress in harmful immune cells in models of multiple sclerosis.
This project builds a model of aging human fat and liver in organ-on-a-chip systems fed with serum from old or young donors.
This project provides tissue labeling and imaging services that help researchers measure cell and tissue changes in mice with metabolic disease.
This project tries to find out how the amount of Trypanosoma cruzi parasite in infected hosts relates to the genes of the parasite.
This project develops a set of bright fluorescent probes that measure the activity of many genes in both thin and thick tissue samples.
This project uses a type of artificial neural network to learn how protein and RNA sequences determine their structure and function.
This project builds tools to track and disturb specific forms of the protein Ras in cancer models to learn how cancer cells resist drug treatment.
This project develops a technique that uses ultrasound scattering to measure the structure of the tiny blood vessels that grow around cancer.
This project develops a machine-learning method to calculate nucleic acid behavior and expands DNA nanotechnology designs for use in therapeutics.
This project studies how microorganisms in the human gut compete for nutrients, a process that is poorly understood.
This project tries to find out how biological networks in cells process and pass on information about their surroundings.
This project analyzes how HIV proteins and antibodies change together in infected rhesus macaques to help design vaccines that trigger broadly neutralizing antibodies.
This project studies how interactions between microbial species change the fitness of mutations and how microbes evolve.
This project builds brain imaging methods that use very high magnetic fields to better link MRI signals to the activity of nerve cells.
This project supports research on aging to improve the health and wellbeing of older adults.
This project builds tiny low-power neural implants placed under the scalp that could monitor and treat brain disorders in real time.
This project studies how the adaptor protein Crk turns immune cell function on and off in human cells and mouse breast cancer models.
This project uses machine learning on imaging data to predict how patients with oropharyngeal cancer will respond to chemo-radiation.
This project builds leukemia mouse models that use immune cells and cancer cells from the same patient to test immunotherapies.
This project provides statistical and genomic data analysis to find progestins that work against endometrial cancer and markers that predict who responds.
